title: 大门口的旋律  (The Tune at the Gate)

segments.t: Qing hurries to the open courtyard gate with Manager Zhou and Teacher Song, calling warmly to the older neighbour who stood listening on Wutong Lane. Listen first.
老先生，您好——要不要进来喝一杯热茶呀？
等等……您是十号门牌小提琴店的老邻居？！
周经理，你们俩认识呀？！
三十年前，每个星期五傍晚六点，他都带着小提琴来这儿！
等等——快看我们的旧明信片：“请给面包师和老师留两把椅子”！
原来他就是当年跟您姑姑合奏星期五二重奏的音乐老师！
他刚才问我，到底是谁终于写完了她那首五月圆舞曲的后半段！
周经理，他隔着窗户听见我写的十六个小节，说了什么？
他眼眶里全是泪水——他说听起来简直就像我姑姑的声音！
您邀请他来参加我们这个星期五傍晚六点的正式开业了吗？！
他答应带上小提琴过来——还要叫上街那头的十位老街坊！
多来十位街坊？！到星期五，小美得准备双倍的黄柠檬啦！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
老先生，您好——要不要进来喝一杯热茶呀？
'Hello, sir—would you like to come inside for a warm cup of tea?' Greeting an elder neighbour at the gate, Qing combines the respectful title "elder mister" with the polite form of "you".
等等……您是十号门牌小提琴店的老邻居？！
'Wait... our old neighbour from the violin shop at number ten?!' Look at how the Mandarin word for "violin" is built: "small hand-carried stringed-instrument", contrasting it with the bigger cello.
周经理，你们俩认识呀？！
'You two know each other, Manager Zhou?!' Unlike English, Mandarin needs no "each other" here—saying "you two know" naturally means you are acquainted.
三十年前，每个星期五傍晚六点，他都带着小提琴来这儿！

'Thirty years ago, every Friday evening at six, he brought his violin here!' In Mandarin, whenever you open with "every Friday", the partner word for "all" appears later before the action to complete the frame.
等等——快看我们的旧明信片：“请给面包师和老师留两把椅子”！

'Wait—look at our old postcard: "Please save two chairs for the baker and the teacher"!' A callback to Episode 1! "Postcard" literally joins "open-letter-card", since the message travels in the open without an envelope.
原来他就是当年跟您姑姑合奏星期五二重奏的音乐老师！
'He was the music teacher who played Friday duets with your aunt back then!' Two musical gems sit side by side: "play-together" for performing in harmony, and "two-fold playing" for a duet.
他刚才问我，到底是谁终于写完了她那首五月圆舞曲的后半段！

'He just asked me who on earth finally finished the second half of her May waltz!' Right before "who", that two-character intensifier literally says "to the very bottom", adding eager curiosity—"who in the world?!"
周经理，他隔着窗户听见我写的十六个小节，说了什么？

'What did he say when he heard my sixteen bars through the window, Manager Zhou?' Teacher Song sounds touchingly hopeful! Musical "bars" in Mandarin are called "small-joints", like sections of bamboo.
他眼眶里全是泪水——他说听起来简直就像我姑姑的声音！
'He had tears in his eyes—he said it sounded just like my aunt's voice!' "Sounded like" literally says "listen-up-come", the everyday twin of "look like" when judging a first impression by ear.
您邀请他来参加我们这个星期五傍晚六点的正式开业了吗？！

'Did you invite him to join our grand opening this Friday evening at six o'clock?!' "Grand opening" uses a crisp two-character business word joining "open" with "enterprise", heard whenever a new shop or cafe launches.
他答应带上小提琴过来——还要叫上街那头的十位老街坊！

'He promised to bring his violin over—and ten old neighbours from down the street!' "Street-lane" is an affectionate word for longtime folks on the same block, warmer than the textbook word for "neighbours".
多来十位街坊？！到星期五，小美得准备双倍的黄柠檬啦！

'Ten extra neighbours?! By Friday, Mei is going to need twice as many yellow lemons!' Placing "more" right before "come" is how Mandarin says "extra people arriving", and "twice as much" is literally "double-fold".
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
老先生，您好——要不要进来喝一杯热茶呀？
等等……您是十号门牌小提琴店的老邻居？！
周经理，你们俩认识呀？！
三十年前，每个星期五傍晚六点，他都带着小提琴来这儿！
等等——快看我们的旧明信片：“请给面包师和老师留两把椅子”！
原来他就是当年跟您姑姑合奏星期五二重奏的音乐老师！
他刚才问我，到底是谁终于写完了她那首五月圆舞曲的后半段！
周经理，他隔着窗户听见我写的十六个小节，说了什么？
他眼眶里全是泪水——他说听起来简直就像我姑姑的声音！
您邀请他来参加我们这个星期五傍晚六点的正式开业了吗？！
他答应带上小提琴过来——还要叫上街那头的十位老街坊！
多来十位街坊？！到星期五，小美得准备双倍的黄柠檬啦！

The Friday duet partner from thirty years ago heard the open window and is bringing his violin—and half the street—back this Friday at six! Episode 5 is complete, and the Season 2 finale awaits. See you next time.
再见！
